original_test_intent: Apply the approved NVQual Test #37 workload to the designated ConnectX or BlueField device for the required thermal interval and verify its temperature rise, steady state, throttling and cooldown remain within approved limits without link/device errors, hang or reboot.
original_method: Bind the NIC/DPU serial, port, BDF and all named temperature sensors; record calibrated sensor provenance, ambient inlet, fan/airflow and idle baseline; pin workload intensity, traffic peer, duration and sampling cadence; collect synchronized sensor, fan, power, throttle, link and error time series continuously; terminate at the approved hard limit or on sensor/cooling fault; preserve evidence and prove controlled return to baseline without disabling protections.
manual_activity: Owner/thermal engineer approves the workload, sensor map, environmental envelope and limits; an operator assures airflow, watches independent telemetry and owns emergency stop and recovery.
required_inputs: Licensed pinned NVQual Test #37 module and compatible ConnectX/BlueField firmware/driver
NIC/DPU serial/port/BDF, traffic peer and canonical sensor/units/calibration map
Load intensity and phases, 120-minute requirement, sample cadence, ambient/inlet and airflow/fan conditions
Warning, throttle and hard-stop limits plus expected cooldown, error acceptance and recovery
safety_requirements: Dedicated SUT, approved thermal window and verified redundant airflow before load
Keep all hardware and firmware thermal protections enabled
Monitor independent BMC/host/device temperature, fan, power, throttle, link and error signals continuously
Stop immediately on sensor loss/disagreement, airflow or fan failure, hard limit, unexpected throttle, link/error burst, hang or reboot
No automatic retry after a thermal or sensor fault
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, sensor provenance, environment, load profile, baselines, limits, stop path and recovery
Run only the approved Test #37 load while continuous telemetry is healthy
Collect the full untruncated heat-up, steady-state and cooldown time series with tool output and platform health
Do not extrapolate missing sensors, disable protection, continue past a limit, repeat a faulted run or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Test #37 load, duration, target and calibrated sensor/environment map
Define thermal/throttle/error limits, stop policy, cooldown endpoint and recovery
Review the complete time series and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It selects the correct thermal module family and temperature source, but lacks workload intensity, duration semantics, canonical sensors, sampling, ambient conditions and limits; a single reading cannot validate thermal dynamics.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run the pinned Test #37 workload only after sensor and airflow validation, capture synchronized heat-up/steady-state/cooldown telemetry for the approved interval, and enforce independent hard stops.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NVQual Test #37, ConnectX/BlueField thermal purpose, all-items/no-hang/no-reboot Criteria, no bundle, and 5/120-minute allocation remain; absent temperatures and load settings are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH CONNECTX BLUEFIELD CONTROLLED THERMAL SOAK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the result as a bounded time-series experiment with known sensor provenance and environment, not a final point sample; correlate device temperature with load, fan, airflow, power, throttling, link and error state through cooldown.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds environmental controls, calibrated sensor binding, continuous sampling, quantitative warning/hard stops and verified recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A module pass or isolated temperature can miss overshoot, oscillation, throttling, sensor dropout, fan response failure and post-load non-recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A two-hour sustained workload can overheat the NIC/DPU or surrounding GPU/PCIe components and can damage availability if cooling or telemetry fails.

project_override_considerations: A substitute load is acceptable only if it produces the approved NIC/DPU thermal power envelope and preserves the same duration, environment, sensor coverage and limits. Synthetic host or GPU stress alone does not replace the target network-device thermal workload.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, approved Test #37 module/configuration and authorization
Target serial/port/BDF, sensor names/units/calibration, ambient/inlet and airflow/fan baseline
Pinned load phases/intensity, duration, sampling and warning/throttle/hard-stop matrix
Complete synchronized temperature, fan, power, throttle, traffic, link and error time series through cooldown
Raw NVQual output plus dmesg/journal, NIC counters, BMC/SEL and thermal-protection state
Abort/recovery or verified stable final idle state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Test #37 Procedure, Criteria and same-row reviews consistently target ConnectX/BlueField thermal qualification. Missing load, sensor and limit details are readiness inputs rather than conflicting intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The thermal purpose is clear. Tooling, calibrated sensors, environment and thresholds are identifiable prerequisites, so the static review is not irreducibly blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2142 Wistron-HGX NV PVP HW-00019-V002: approve the pinned NVQual Test #37 workload, ConnectX/BlueField serial/port/BDF and sensor calibration map, traffic/load phases and 120-minute duration, sample cadence, ambient/airflow/fan/power conditions, warning/throttle/hard-stop and error limits, cooldown endpoint, aborts, and recovery.

review_improvement: Turns a generic thermal module result into a controlled two-hour thermal time-series qualification with environmental controls, independent limits and proof of cooldown.
independent_technical_reasoning: Thermal acceptance depends on the complete response curve: peak overshoot, equilibrium, throttle transitions and cooldown may fail even when one sampled temperature is acceptable. Sensor identity and ambient airflow directly affect interpretation. Therefore the case requires synchronized calibrated time-series data and an independent stop path; a sensor or cooling failure ends the run immediately because continued loading would remove the safety basis.
